newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway, Russia sign humanitarian aid pact.
newsitem.headline: Norway, Russia sign humanitarian aid pact.

text.p: Norway and Russia on Thursday signed a co-operation agreement for humanitarian aid, according to NTB news agency.
The first joint-relief projects will begin in a few weeks in Angola and Rwanda, the agency said.

"This agreement is a good example that the Cold War is over, and Norway and Russia can together help suffering people in the Third World," it quoted Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal as saying after signing the document.

Sergei Shoigu, Russian Minister for Civil Defence and Emergencies, on a two-day visit to the Norwegian capital, said: "This is a practical document that will lead to action. We will begin the relief work in the near future."

Norway and Russia collaborated in the airlift to Belgrade in rump Yugoslavia in 1995 and have worked together on the Arctic island of Spitzbergen, which Norway has ruled under the terms of a 1920s international treaty, although many other nations, including Russia, have the right to exploit the coal resources there.
A spokesman for the Norwegian Foreign Ministry said it was the first formal co-operation agreement for humanitarian purposes that either of the countries had entered.
In Angola, where Norway is already active, they will work to clear mines, while in Rwanda the Scandinavian nation will reinforce ongoing Russian projects, especially in the field of transport.
